ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C = 90^\circ$, $\angle A = 20^\circ$, $BD$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$, then what is the measure of $\angle BDC$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle A=20^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle ABC=180^\circ-\angle C-\angle A=70^\circ$,\\
since $BD$ is the bisector of $\angle ABC$,\\
thus $\angle DBC=\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC=35^\circ$,\\
in $\triangle DBC$,\\
since $\angle C=90^\circ$, $\angle DBC=35^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BDC=180^\circ-\angle C-\angle DBC=\boxed{55^\circ}$.
